text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- International environment organisation Greenpeace demonstrated on Wednesday in Denmark's second largest city Aarhus against a South Korean freighter partly loaded with genetically engineered soya beans.

--- Denmark is to participate with Canada, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Sweden and Austria in the U.N. Stand-by Forces High Readiness Brigade (SHIRBRIG), to be brought into action with 15 to 30 days notice in crisis areas. Heading the brigade of some 4,000 soldiers will be a Danish officer while the different units will be based in their own countries with headquarters in northern Zealand.

--- Organisers of Copenhagen's year as European Union Cultural Capital 1996, see the project as a success based on a Gallup poll. According to Gallup the project brought 400,000 more hotel stays to the capital than in 1995 and 7-10 million tickets to Cultural Capital events were sold.
--- The government is to give 21 million crowns to local authorities in support of payments to private home help companies.

--- Opposition Liberal Party leader Uffe Elleman Jensen does not believe in a future Liberal-Conservative- Progress Party government, but foresees new parliamentary elections next spring which will be a personal struggle between himself and prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen.
